# Kybl: one file manager for every cloud, bucket and server

Kybl is a free app for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iPhone that puts object storage, cloud drives, servers and your own disk side by side in one window. Website: https://kybl.app/

## Connections

- Object storage: Amazon S3 and any S3-compatible endpoint (Cloudflare R2, Hetzner Object Storage, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO, Ceph), Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage and Kybl Storage.
- Cloud drives: Google Drive (My Drive, shared drives, Shared with me), OneDrive and Dropbox, signed in through the browser.
- Servers: SFTP (password, key or SSH agent, host keys checked), SSH (an SFTP connection that opens as a terminal), FTP and FTPS, and WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud, NAS boxes).
- Your computer: your own folders and drives, in the same panes.

Presets fill in endpoints, regions and each provider's quirks, and every connection can be tested before saving. Import connections reads FileZilla's Site Manager and ~/.ssh/config (LocalForward lines become SSH tunnels); folders become sidebar groups. Passwords and keys are stored in an encrypted vault whose key lives in the operating system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, a Linux Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring or KWallet, the Android Keystore on phones). They are never written to a settings file, and Kybl talks to your storage and servers directly.

## Features

- Panes and workspaces: up to six panes split any way, with commander keys (F5 copy, F6 move, F7 new folder, F8 delete) and synchronized browsing. Each layout is a workspace tab, and a layout can be saved as a recipe.
- Copy between anything: drag files from one connection to another, or start a copy or move job for whole folders. Jobs check sizes, keep their place across restarts and use server-side copies where the provider has them.
- Thumbnails in a blink: Cloud drives hand over their own thumbnails; elsewhere a JPEG's embedded EXIF thumbnail is read from only the first 256 KB when it has one, otherwise the image is fetched and resized. Thumbnails are cached on disk.
- Previews in place: images, video, audio, PDF and text open in Quick Look (Space), with Get Info (Cmd+I).
- Edit anywhere (desktop): open a remote file in any app; each save uploads back, and with the recommended setting a change on the server meanwhile stops the upload so you can overwrite, keep both or reload. Files up to 100 MB. Kybl also has its own editor.
- Batch rename: rename many files at once with a pattern (name, number, date, extension) or find and replace (regex too), with a preview that flags clashes.
- Archives and diffs: zip and unzip (on the server over SSH when it can), open archives like folders, compare two files or two folders.
- Search that digs: paged loading for folders with hundreds of thousands of items, search through every subfolder, and search inside files on your computer and SSH or SFTP servers.
- Transfer queue: speed and time left, pause, speed limits, retry, resume after a restart on most connections, and optional size or checksum checks.
- Share links: expiring links on S3, OneDrive and Dropbox.
- Command palette (Cmd+K) and keyboard shortcuts for everything.
- Custom actions: your own shell commands on selected files, with placeholders and a shortcut, run on your computer or on an SSH or SFTP server.
- Make it yours: light, dark or system theme, colour schemes and accents, fonts, text size and density.
- On your phone too: the same connections on Android and iPhone with a touch interface, photo backup to any connection, background transfers on Android and an app lock.

## What works with which connection

- Works with every connection: browse, upload, download, delete, copy and move between connections, thumbnails and Quick Look, zip and unzip, search subfolders by name. In the computer app also: folder sync and mirror, editing in your own app, and mounting as a drive (macOS and Linux).
- Rename: S3, Azure and Google Cloud Storage rename by copying, so it is slower. The others rename directly.
- Copy inside a connection without downloading: S3, Azure and Google Cloud Storage (same container), Google Drive, OneDrive (same drive), Dropbox, WebDAV and your computer. Not SFTP or FTP.
- Uploads continue after a restart: S3, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, SFTP and FTP. On Azure, Google Cloud Storage and WebDAV the upload starts again.
- Share links that expire: S3 (only people with the link can open it), OneDrive and Dropbox (public until the link ends, if it lasts over 1 hour on OneDrive or 4 hours on Dropbox; Dropbox needs a paid plan for this). Not Google Drive, Azure, Google Cloud Storage, SFTP, FTP or WebDAV.
- Deleted files can be restored: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox and your computer. On the others, delete is permanent.
- Change permissions: SFTP, and FTP servers that allow it. Tags, storage class and metadata: S3.
- Search inside files: your computer and SSH or SFTP servers.
- Terminal: SSH and SFTP servers, and your computer (macOS, Linux, and Windows with PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL or Git Bash). SSH tunnels and your own commands on the server: SSH and SFTP only. Your own commands on your computer can use files from any connection (downloaded first).
- Phone app: browse, preview, upload, download, share and back up photos, with every connection. Terminal, tunnels, folder sync, drives and editing in other apps are in the computer app only. Drives are not on Windows yet.

## SSH and terminals (desktop)

- An SSH connection opens a terminal on the server with one click; its Folders button opens the server's files above the terminal.
- Terminal panes on your computer (macOS, Linux, and Windows with PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL or Git Bash) or any SSH or SFTP server, saved with workspaces, with a "follow the folder above" option.
- SSH tunnels (local port forwards) to reach a database or admin panel behind the server, with auto-start.
- Pasting several lines asks first and shows exactly what will run.

## Sync, mirror and drives (desktop)

- Folder sync between a folder on your computer and any connection: upload, download or two-way. Changes on your computer are picked up within seconds and the other side is checked every few minutes (5 by default), ignore rules skip node_modules, .DS_Store and friends, big deletions ask first, and a file changed on both sides keeps both versions. It keeps running from the menu bar or system tray with the window closed, unless you turn that off.
- Mirror: deploy a folder to a server (or pull one down) with a dry run first, then re-run a saved mirror in one click.
- Mount as a drive: any connection, bucket or folder appears in Finder (macOS) or the Linux file manager.

## Kybl Storage

No bucket yet? Kybl Storage is S3 storage run by Kybl. Sign in with your email at https://app.kybl.app/, approve the app in the browser (or with a code on another device) and it connects itself, with no access keys to copy or endpoint to type. The free plan has 10 GB; bigger plans are coming. Data is stored in the EU. The dashboard shows usage and devices, and makes access keys for any other S3 tool.

Encryption at rest: every file is encrypted with its bucket's own key (AES-256, SSE-C) before it is written to disk. The storage provider, its staff, its backups and anyone holding only the storage side see ciphertext, and reads without the key fail. File names and sizes stay visible there. It is not end-to-end: Kybl's servers encrypt files as they pass through, so data that only you should read is best encrypted before uploading.

## Download

- macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel builds
- Windows: 64-bit installer
- Linux: AppImage, .deb or .rpm
- Android: Kybl.apk (Android 7 or newer), installed straight from the download; Google Play later.
- iPhone and iPad: Kybl.ipa for sideloading (not in the App Store). Add the source https://github.com/erikkubica/kybl/releases/latest/download/altstore-source.json in AltStore or SideStore, or install the .ipa with Sideloadly. A free Apple ID signs it for 7 days; AltStore and SideStore renew it.

On first launch on a Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway (the app is signed but not yet notarized). On Windows, if SmartScreen warns, click More info > Run anyway.

## FAQ

Q: What can Kybl connect to?
A: Object storage: Amazon S3 and any S3-compatible endpoint (Cloudflare R2, Hetzner, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO, Ceph), Azure Blob Storage and Google Cloud Storage. Cloud drives: Google Drive, OneDrive and Dropbox. Servers: SFTP, SSH, FTP and FTPS, and WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud, NAS boxes). And the files on your own computer or phone, all side by side.

Q: Is Kybl free?
A: Yes. Kybl is a free download for macOS, Windows, Linux, Android and iPhone. Use your own storage and servers as usual, or start with 10 GB free on Kybl Storage.

Q: Can I use Kybl as an SSH client?
A: Yes. Add an SSH connection and a click opens a terminal on the server, with a Folders button for its files. Any SFTP connection can also open a terminal, start SSH tunnels (local port forwards) and run your own commands on the server. Terminals are in the computer app, on macOS, Windows and Linux, for servers and for your own computer.

Q: Can I bring my FileZilla sites or SSH hosts?
A: Yes. Import connections reads FileZilla's Site Manager and your ~/.ssh/config (including LocalForward lines, which become tunnels). Folders become sidebar groups, and FileZilla's saved passwords and key files go straight into Kybl's encrypted vault (an SSH config holds no passwords; its keys are used where they are).

Q: Can Kybl sync a folder?
A: Yes, with any connection: upload, download or two-way. Changes on your computer go up within seconds and the other side is checked every few minutes; Kybl skips what your ignore rules say, asks before big deletions, keeps both versions when a file changed on both sides, and keeps syncing from the menu bar or system tray with the window closed (unless you turn that off). For deploys, Mirror shows a dry run before it touches anything.

Q: Where are my passwords and keys stored?
A: In an encrypted vault on your device, with its key in the operating system keychain: the macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or a Secret Service such as GNOME Keyring on Linux (the Android Keystore on phones). Never in a settings file, and Kybl talks to your storage and servers directly.

Q: What is Kybl Storage?
A: S3 storage run by Kybl for people without a bucket of their own. Sign in with your email, approve the app in the browser and it connects itself, with no access keys to copy. The free plan has 10 GB, stored in the EU, and your dashboard can make access keys for any other S3 tool.

Q: Are my files on Kybl Storage encrypted?
A: Yes, at rest. Every file is encrypted with its bucket's own key (AES-256) before it is written to disk, so the storage provider, its staff and its backups only ever see ciphertext. It is not end-to-end: Kybl's servers encrypt files as they pass through, so for data only you should read, encrypt it before uploading.

Q: Does Kybl handle very large files and folders?
A: Yes. Large files go up in parts on S3 and cloud drives, uploads resume after a restart on S3, cloud drives, SFTP and FTP, folders with hundreds of thousands of items load page by page, and search looks through every subfolder, or inside files on your computer and SSH or SFTP servers.
